runs.v: New Jersey installations follow the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, and local building codes mandate flashing at roof-wall intersections and other vulnerable areas. Step flashing overlaps each shingle by at least 2 inches, counter-flashing overlaps the base flashing by at least 3 to 4 inches, and a drip edge extends at least 2 inches onto the deck, fastened no more than 12 inches on center with at least 2-inch end laps, per IRC Section R905.2.8.5. Ice-and-water protection, a self-adhered membrane that self-seals around fasteners, per ASTM D1970, goes at the eaves, valleys, and penetrations, the vulnerable areas of northern New Jersey roofs; high-grade sealant is used only where required.

runs.v: Flashing should last as long as the roof around it, yet rubber pipe boots and caulked joints fail years sooner, and galvanized steel corrodes where moisture sits against it, which is why corrosion-resistant metals are essential in New Jersey's climate. Choosing compatible materials prevents galvanic corrosion between dissimilar metals, and a copper chimney detail that has served Bloomfield winters for decades may still be sound. Asphalt shingles are commonly used on Bloomfield roofs, slate is a premium roofing option, metal roofing can last up to 50 years, EPDM flat roofing typically lasts 20–25 years, and TPO membrane systems are popular for commercial flat roofs. What is the 25% rule for roofing? In New Jersey it is a permit line: on buildings other than detached one- and two-family houses, repairing more than 25% of the roof within 12 months needs a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Roofers also use it as a planning rule: once damage covers more than about a quarter of the roof, roof replacement usually beats another repair, and new flashing goes in with the new covering. faqs.q: How do Bloomfield homeowners know if a leak is a flashing problem or a shingle problem?

runs.v: Leaks at chimney, skylight, roof-to-wall, or valley locations are almost always flashing failures, per the NRCA-attributed estimate above; a stain below the middle of a uniform roof plane points to the shingles instead.

faqs.q: Does flashing replacement require removing shingles on my Bloomfield home?

runs.v: Yes, in most cases: step flashing weaves one piece per shingle course and valley flashing sits beneath the shingles, so the shingles at the transition are lifted, then reinstalled to match.

faqs.q: Does flashing work on a Bloomfield home need a permit or historic approval?

runs.v: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in NJ? Most roof repairs in Bloomfield do not require a permit: under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 of the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, roof covering repair or replacement on a detached one- or two-family house, flashing included, is ordinary maintenance. A commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a permit once the work exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months, and changes to the roof structure may require building permits. A property in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the Bloomfield construction office before work begins.

faqs.q: Why does my Bloomfield split-level leak at the step-down between roof levels?

runs.v: That step-down is a roof-to-wall intersection; without step flashing and a kickout diverter, water runs behind the siding into the wall, per IRC Section R903.2.1. The fix adds an ice-and-water membrane, woven step flashing, and a kickout, then reinstalls the siding, per InterNACHI guidance.

faqs.q: What flashing material lasts on a Bloomfield roof?

runs.v: Corrosion-resistant aluminum or copper outlasts the galvanized steel found on Bloomfield's pre-war stock, because galvanized flashing corrodes where moisture sits against concealed metal beneath shingles and behind siding.

faqs.q: How do I fix the flashing on my roof?

runs.v: Hire a professional: flashing work means lifting shingles and lapping metal correctly, and a caulk-only patch is temporary. A proper fix removes the shingles around the joint, replaces damaged flashing with new metal lapped over the course below, and reinstalls the covering.
